traits.note: FNA vol. 27, Ceratodon (McIntosh; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants in loose to dense tufts, turfs or mats, green to yellow-green, often tinged red-brown or purple; stems (0.2-)1-3(-4) cm; leaves contorted or somewhat crisped when dry; seta red, purplish, yellow or yellow-orange, twisted when dry; capsule erect to inclined or horizontal, dark red to purplish brown. C. purpureus (same volume): leaves 0.35-2.8 mm; seta 1-3(-4) cm; capsule (1-)2-2.5(-3) mm, in subsp. purpureus inclined to horizontal, red to purplish. Wikipedia, Ceratodon purpureus (read 2026-11-05): on disturbed sites, old roofs, sidewalk cracks, burned ground; most abundant on exposed dry mineral soil; setae turn red in spring.

traits.leaf_shape.note: FNA vol. 27, Ceratodon purpureus (efloras, read 2026-11-05): leaves lanceolate, ovate-lanceolate, or triangular-lanceolate.

traits.leaf_dry_crisping.note: FNA vol. 27, Ceratodon purpureus (efloras, read 2026-11-05): leaves erect-patent to contorted or somewhat crisped, rarely straight when dry; 'somewhat crisped' is 0.5 by the trait's scale.

traits.capsule_share.note: Dioicous but fruiting freely on roofs and burned ground (Wikipedia); estimate.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Lanceolate leaves about a quarter to a third as wide as long (FNA's lanceolate).

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate for a pioneer turf on open ground; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.

traits.capsule_shape.note: FNA vol. 27, Ceratodon purpureus: capsule oblong to long-cylindric. (efloras, read 2026-11-05)

traits.operculum_form.note: FNA vol. 27, Ceratodon: operculum conic to long-conic, straight. (efloras, read 2026-11-05)

traits.older_leaf_colour.note: FNA vol. 27, Ceratodon purpureus (read 2026-11-05): plants in open to dense tufts or turfs, green to yellowish, often tinged reddish brown or purple. The colour is ours for that tinge, on the older leaves below the green tips.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, about 20 a taxon, script moss_colour.py): the median linear r/g and b/g of the moss pixels (C. purpureus r/g 0.92, b/g 0.20). Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible (Lovelock and Robinson 2002, Plant Cell Environ. 25: 1239, Antarctic Grimmia; moss biocrust albedo about 0.11 against 0.20 for bare soil, Sci. Total Environ. 2020), the canopy's own shade darkening the shell further.

traits.spore_diameter_m.note: FNA vol. 27, Ceratodon purpureus (McIntosh; efloras, read 2026-11-05): spores (10-)11-14(-17) µm.
